question: Should OpenClaw add a read-only recursive/depth mode to `subagents list`, and should it live in the existing `subagents` tool/slash command or wait for broader session-chain/tree APIs?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates public model-facing and slash-command semantics around nested agent hierarchy visibility and control boundaries.

options.title: Add Read-Only Depth Listing
options.body: Add an additive `depth` or `recursive` option that returns descendant rows with parent/depth metadata while leaving mutation scope unchanged.

options.title: Fold Into Chain Or Tree Work
options.body: Keep this issue open but make recursive list output depend on the broader session-chain or active-agent tree design before adding another public shape.

options.title: Decline Hierarchy Expansion
options.body: Document current direct-child visibility and descendant summary behavior if maintainers do not want depth-0 inspection of depth-2 workers in core.

recommendation.title: Add Read-Only Depth Listing
recommendation.body: Add an additive `depth` or `recursive` option that returns descendant rows with parent/depth metadata while leaving mutation scope unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the nested subagent orchestration and subagents tool surface that this product decision would extend.
